name: IBM
summary: IBM hires for consulting, software, infrastructure and research roles, and its careers site describes the usual steps: application, screening, one or two online assessments depending on the role (such as a coding test, a recorded video interview or an English test), interviews and a decision. IBM says it uses structured or behavioural interviews, and for entry-level developers candidates commonly report a technical interview followed by a behavioural round with management.
looks_for: Trust and personal responsibility in all relationships
Explaining your reasoning, not just the final answer

covers: Your background in two or three sentences: studies or current role
One or two things you've built or achieved that fit this role
Why you're interested in IBM and this team now

questions.text: Tell me about a time you learned a new technology for a project.
covers: Why the project needed it and how much time you had
How you learned it: docs, small experiments, asking others
What you delivered with it and what you'd learn differently now

questions.text: How would you explain a technical idea to a client who isn't technical?
covers: Starting from what the client cares about: cost, risk, time
An everyday comparison instead of jargon, with an example
Checking they understood and inviting questions

questions.text: Tell me about a time you put a client's or user's success ahead of the easier option for you.
covers: What the easy option was and why it fell short for them
What the extra effort involved
The outcome for the client or user

questions.text: Tell me about a mistake you made that affected others. How did you take responsibility?
covers: The mistake and who it affected, stated plainly
How quickly you told people and what you did to fix it
What you changed so it wouldn't happen again

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with people from another team or country to deliver something.
covers: The goal and who was involved
A difficulty, such as time zones or different priorities, and how you handled it
What was delivered and what you learned about working across teams

questions.text: Explain the difference between public, private and hybrid cloud, and why a company might choose hybrid.
covers: Public: shared provider infrastructure; private: dedicated to one organisation
Hybrid: both, working together
Reasons for hybrid: regulation, existing systems, cost, keeping some data in-house

questions.text: What is a container, and how does a platform like Kubernetes help run containers at scale?
covers: A container packages an app with what it needs to run the same way anywhere
How it differs from a virtual machine
What Kubernetes adds: scheduling, scaling, restarts and rolling updates

questions.text: Walk me through your final-year project or a recent project: the problem, your part and what you'd improve.
covers: The problem and why it mattered
Your own part, the technology and one hard decision
Results, and what you'd improve with more time

questions.text: A client wants to use AI to answer its customers' questions. What would you ask before recommending an approach?
covers: The business goal and how success will be measured
The data available, privacy rules and what must never go wrong
Starting small with a pilot, with people checking answers

questions.text: What does ACID mean for a database, and why does it matter for a bank's transactions?
covers: Atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, each in a plain line
A money transfer as the example: both sides happen or neither does
What could go wrong without these guarantees

questions.text: Why IBM, and which part of its business interests you most: consulting, software or infrastructure?
covers: Something specific you know about IBM's work
The area you chose and why it suits your skills
What you hope to learn there

questions.text: Where do you see yourself in five years, and how would IBM help you get there?
covers: A realistic direction, such as deeper technical skill or client leadership
Steps you'd take, including learning and certifications
How this role is the right first step

tips: IBM's careers site says the online stage may include a coding test, a recorded video interview or an English test, depending on the role; check your invite for which ones apply.
For a work-style questionnaire, answer as you really are and go with your first instinct, as IBM's assessment FAQ suggests.
Explain your reasoning in assessments and interviews, not just the final answer; IBM's own advice for entry-level developers says this.
In the technical interview, be honest about gaps and say how you'd learn the topic.
Prepare questions about client work, learning and career growth for the end of the interview.

sources.title: Entry level developer: becoming a successful candidate (ibm.com)
